published.citation: Zhou et al. 2015, dayside brightness temperature at 2.159 µm (NASA Exoplanet Archive emission table): 2200 +/- 100 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015MNRAS.454.3002Z/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 2.159 µm (Anglo Australian Telescope IRIS2) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: 1 measured of 1 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength
